title: The Galois Correspondence for ℂ / ℝ
description: The Galois-theoretic route to the no-intermediate-fields theorem for ℝ ⊆ ℂ: ℂ/ℝ is a Galois extension with Gal(ℂ/ℝ) ≅ ℤ/2ℤ (generated by complex conjugation), and the fundamental theorem of Galois theory's bijection between intermediate fields and subgroups — together with the fact that a group of prime order 2 has only the trivial subgroups — shows every intermediate field is ℝ or ℂ.

overview.historicalContext: The parent entry (fundamental-theorem-algebra-oq-04, "ℂ is the Unique Algebraic Closure of ℝ") proves there are no proper intermediate fields between ℝ and ℂ using the tower law: [ℂ:ℝ] = [ℂ:K]·[K:ℝ] = 2 forces [K:ℝ] ∈ {1,2}. This entry answers that entry's third open question by giving the alternative, structural proof through Galois theory — the same conclusion read off the subgroup lattice of Gal(ℂ/ℝ) rather than from a degree count.
overview.problemStatement: Prove the Galois correspondence for ℂ/ℝ: intermediate fields correspond bijectively to subgroups of Gal(ℂ/ℝ) ≅ ℤ/2ℤ, giving an alternative proof that there are no intermediate fields.
overview.proofStrategy: Four moves. (1) Establish IsGalois ℝ ℂ from normality (ℂ = ℝ̄ gives Normal ℝ ℂ via IsAlgClosure) and separability (automatic in char 0). (2) Compute |Gal(ℂ/ℝ)| = [ℂ:ℝ] = 2 using IsGalois.card_aut_eq_finrank, then conclude cyclicity (≅ ℤ/2ℤ) from isCyclic_of_prime_card. (3) Invoke the fundamental theorem of Galois theory (IsGalois.intermediateFieldEquivSubgroup) as an order-reversing bijection between intermediate fields and subgroups. (4) Enumerate the subgroups of the order-2 group via Lagrange (only ⊥ and ⊤), and transport that back across the order-reversing bijection to conclude every intermediate field is ⊥ = ℝ or ⊤ = ℂ. The work concentrates entirely in the group side; the field side is read off the lattice.
keyInsights: ℂ/ℝ is Galois: char 0 gives separability, and ℂ being an algebraic closure of ℝ gives normality.
For a Galois extension, |Aut| equals the degree, so |Gal(ℂ/ℝ)| = 2; a group of order 2 is cyclic, hence ≅ ℤ/2ℤ.
The fundamental theorem of Galois theory is an order-reversing bijection between intermediate fields and subgroups.
A prime-order group has exactly two subgroups (⊥ and ⊤) by Lagrange — this is what 'no intermediate fields' becomes on the group side.
The correspondence reverses order: ⊤ (field) ↦ ⊥ (subgroup) and ⊥ (field) ↦ ⊤ (subgroup), so each intermediate field is pinned to ⊥=ℝ or ⊤=ℂ.
prerequisites: Galois theory (Galois extensions, the fundamental theorem)
Group theory (Lagrange's theorem, cyclic groups of prime order)

conclusion.summary: ℂ/ℝ is a Galois extension whose group is cyclic of order 2 (generated by complex conjugation). Through the fundamental theorem of Galois theory, the two subgroups of this prime-order group (⊥ and ⊤) correspond to the only two intermediate fields, ℝ and ℂ. This gives a structural, lattice-theoretic alternative to the parent entry's tower-law proof of no-intermediate-fields.
conclusion.implications: Reading the no-intermediate-fields theorem off the subgroup lattice rather than from a degree count is the conceptual gain: it makes 'no intermediate field' synonymous with 'no proper nontrivial subgroup,' a purely group-theoretic fact that needs nothing about ℂ beyond |Gal| = 2. The same template — Galois ⇒ correspondence ⇒ subgroup lattice — scales to any prime-degree extension and underlies the Galois-theoretic proofs of insolubility (Abel–Ruffini) and ruler-and-compass impossibilities. It also exhibits the order reversal of the correspondence concretely: the maximal field ℂ pairs with the trivial group, the minimal field ℝ with the whole group.
